findings.title: Guidance as a graciously delivered gift
findings.claim: The focus retains ordinary right-direction language, while its coordination with mercy allows guidance to be heard as a gracious benefit delivered to those addressed, not only as information.
findings.mechanism: The focus word huda carries right guidance; raḥma places it beside inward concern that issues in care. The attributed 31:4 granting and 31:5 source cues, together with 49:17's explicit bestowal of guidance, make the gift image contact the focus pair. The image changes the emphasis from an abstract direction alone to direction received as favor.
findings.reader_payoff: Readers can perceive orientation as a relation of nearness and care, while still keeping its directional content.
findings.containment: H-D-Y B004 is an image activated by giving language and 49:17, not an exclusive lexical gloss for huda. The local 31:4–5 details are reported by legacy support rather than supplied as target Arabic here. Gift does not mean a transaction or an earned entitlement; reward remains a possible wider counter-reading.

epistemic.reason: A trusted focus publication and an exact wider 49:17 target support the central relation; the 31:4–5 details and part of the gift interpretation are legacy-attributed, and target morphology is not supplied.

findings.mechanism: Huda carries direction/course, and muhsinin carries good action and a positively evaluated quality. The distinct later counsel about walking and lowering the voice (31:18–19), followed by the self-surrendering muhsin at 31:22, returns through those carriers and changes direction from abstract information into enacted comportment.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see inward orientation in an ordinary body's manner without reducing the focus to a rule about walking or speaking.
findings.containment: The measured-conduct texts illustrate rather than define guidance, beauty, or ihsan; 31:18 itself is supplied here through legacy support, while the 31:19 and 31:22 connection rows give exact target Arabic. The composed-bearing inference remains qualified.

epistemic.reason: The focus claim has trusted support, and the wider 31:19/22 texts are exact, but the detailed comportment reading is also carried by legacy support and contextual inference.

findings.title: Gifted recipients remain active responders
findings.claim: The focus's good-doers are not merely passive recipients: guidance and mercy can be bestowed without being earned, while the recipients answer through intentional worship and sound deeds. Beneficence disposes one to receive direction as a gift; it does not purchase it.
findings.mechanism: The paired focus nouns are assigned to the good-doers; the independent 49:17 bestowal and 29:69 striving-to-guidance sequence make gift and response meet. The attributed 31:4/8 cues name the recipients' prayer, giving, faith, and sound action, returning the relation through huda, raḥma, and muhsinin. Thus the reading changes from passive allocation to gracious provision met by active response.
findings.reader_payoff: The recipient can be both dependent on divine guidance and responsible for an enacted response, without turning practice into a price for the gift.
findings.containment: The relation between the dative and the paired nouns remains syntactically open: recipient, suitability, and constitutive readings are not collapsed. The 31:4/8 detail is legacy-attributed, and the response reading is an inference rather than a claim that action earns guidance.

epistemic.reason: The reading is a legacy-unbound inference whose main wider triggers are supplied as exact Arabic at 49:17 and 29:69; the cited 31:4/8 details are attributed and the dative relation remains open.

findings.title: Mercy and ihsan as bounded repair
findings.claim: The wider legal-relief scene makes mercy and ihsan concrete as repair that protects a relationship while retaining a boundary: pardon is followed by fair pursuit and good payment, and aggression beyond that limit is condemned. The giving, anger-restraint, and pardon in 3:134 offer a parallel active profile of muhsinin.
findings.mechanism: The focus raḥma and muhsinin are the carriers; 2:178 independently names relief, mercy, and payment with ihsan in a bounded pardon process, while 3:134 names generosity, restraint of anger, and pardon before calling their agents muhsinin. These wider acts return through both focus words and shift mercy from affect alone to accountable, restorative conduct.
findings.reader_payoff: Mercy appears neither as indulgence nor as detached feeling: it can enable repair and generosity while refusing excess and preserving responsibility.
findings.containment: This is a contextual resonance, not a claim that 31:3 is a legal verse or that every case follows the exact procedure of 2:178. The registry supplies exact target Arabic but not target morphology; the examples do not exhaust mercy or ihsan.

epistemic.reason: The Quranic target text is supplied exactly in both connection records, but their morphology is not; the cross-text reading is a bounded contextual inference.

findings.title: Mercy as a gestational ecology of care
findings.claim: Across 31:10, 31:14, 31:16, and 31:34, the HFT trace reads mercy as an inferred ecology of stabilization, hidden carrying, weakness, emergence, and separation, with guidance operating inside conditions that hold vulnerable growth until it can emerge. The same trace treats good action as care that sustains formation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are huda, womb-like raḥma, and beneficent action. Firm establishment and instability in 31:10, pregnancy, weakness and weaning in 31:14, hidden minuteness in 31:16, and the explicit womb reference in 31:34 are the distinct context triggers; they return through the focus direction, mercy, and good-doer words and change mercy from feeling beside direction into costly, protective conditions for growth.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive care as material and temporal: stabilizing, carrying, protecting, and eventually allowing separation rather than enclosing indefinitely.
findings.containment: The ecology is a material analogy and the support itself allows these scenes to remain parallel examples instead of one exclusive lexical specification. Context roots, roles, and indices without an independent focus branch record remain attributed; they do not acquire invented glosses or facets. The focus womb branch is activated contextually by the explicit womb and carrying cues, not asserted as the only sense of raḥma.

epistemic.reason: The anchors have exact Arabic and complete coverage, but the unity of a gestational ecology is explicitly a reader inference and the contextual root/facet assignments are attributed.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can value family care without confusing closeness with transferred moral standing.

findings.title: Ihsan under effortful pressure
findings.claim: The focus muhsinin can be pressure-tested by asking whether good action remains directed when effort is costly and resolve is required. This is an analogical stress test of ihsan, not its primary morphology.
findings.mechanism: The focus active participle muhsinin is the carrier, and the unusual HSN B005 effort/limit branch supplies the analogical pressure point. The independent hardship/exertion at 31:15 and resolve at 31:17 contact that carrier and change an easy-polish image into a question about sustained good action under strain.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that active goodness may be tested not only by ease but by persistence when capacity is pressed.
findings.containment: B005 is restricted to two fixed expressions and must not be generalized to all effort or every endpoint. Because muhsinin is not one of those expressions, the branch is used only as a bounded analogy, never as an ordinary lexical gloss. The two contextual roots/roles remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT candidate explicitly marks this as an outlier and the focus B005 branch has a narrow fixed-expression boundary; the pressure relation is analogical.
